whyItMatters: This rule captures the actual takeover condition: a distribution still points to an S3 origin bucket that does not exist. Once this state exists, name reuse can turn it into content takeover.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may monitor for orphaned origin names and claim them when the bucket name becomes available.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This class of exposure usually results from stale infrastructure references rather than an attacker API action, which is why posture analytics are essential.
threatContext.whyItMatters: Unlike precursor detections, this rule identifies the directly exploitable misconfiguration state itself.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, trusted CloudFront distributions may serve content from a bucket later controlled by a different party.

requiredLogSources: S3 bucket existence validation or bucket inventory
Optional CloudTrail for origin configuration changes
loggingRequirements: The posture job must enumerate CloudFront distributions regularly.
The platform must correctly identify which origins correspond to S3 buckets.
Bucket-existence checks such as `HeadBucket` must run in a controlled and reliable way.
limitations: This is a posture control, not a pure event-driven rule.
Not every origin-looking hostname is an S3 bucket that can be reclaimed the same way.
Cross-account ownership checks may require additional validation beyond simple existence testing.

rawToNormalized.notes: Whether the origin bucket currently exists

enrichment.description: Determine whether the origin bucket exists and whether it is controlled by the expected owner.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Distinguishes exploitable state from normal operation.

enrichment.description: Classify whether the affected distribution is public, customer-facing, or internal.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Prioritizes the most dangerous orphaned origins.

enrichment.description: Confirm that the origin truly maps to an S3 bucket path susceptible to this failure mode.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Prevents false positives on unrelated origins.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should run as scheduled posture analytics: enumerate CloudFront distributions, extract S3-backed origin bucket names, and flag any distribution whose referenced bucket no longer exists or is no longer controlled as expected.
conditions: distribution inventory contains an S3-backed origin
referenced bucket name does not currently exist or fails expected ownership validation
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Normalize S3 origin hostnames carefully. 2. Re-run the posture job on a regular cadence. 3. Prioritize distributions with public aliases or business-critical traffic.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when a CloudFront distribution references an S3 origin bucket that is missing or otherwise orphaned.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low with accurate origin parsing and bucket validation

whereItRuns: Lambda or Step Functions inventory checks
deployment.scheduling: Run on a regular schedule and after distribution or bucket lifecycle changes.
considerations: This is the core posture detector for the orphaned-origin family.
Reliable origin parsing and bucket validation are the main dependencies.
